top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before April.
61ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo. Practice on paved road through coastal hills and agricultural: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 90 miles.
At mile 60 of 90, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
5,500ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
5,500ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,500ft of climbing on paved road through coastal hills and agricultural does to your power file on race day.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved road through coastal hills and agricultural can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 90 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.

race_overlay.weather: April in Monterey, California, USA — Mid-April on the Monterey coast delivers near-perfect cycling weather. Morning fog burns off by 9 AM, giving way to sunshine and temperatures in the 55-70F range. The inland Salinas Valley can push into the mid-70s by afternoon. Wind is the wildcard: Pacific headwinds on the return leg through Carmel Valley can hit 15-20 mph. Rain is unlikely but not impossible in April. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo’s 90 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Sea Otter Classic Gran Fondo rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on paved road through coastal hills and agricultural valley to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, TT Threshold, and Road Specific to prepare you for 90 miles of paved road through coastal hills and agricultural valley in Monterey, California, USA.
